title: Allow for named base URLs so that relative links can be used for multiple websites or subsites

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body: ### What problem are you trying to solve? Sometimes a website might have a subsite or multiple that are frequently linked to on a page. It would be nice to be able to use relative URLs for these links instead of needing to write out the entire absolute URL. It doesn’t make sense to use the base URL set with the `` element for this since that might be needed for the main site and there might be multiple base URLs that a website wants to use (i.e. today you can only set one base URL). ### What solutions exist today? Today, this would need to be solved at the server or JavaScript-level. ### How would you solve it? This question seems to go against the “Forget the solution” advice in the FAQ, but since you’re asking: This seems like an opportunity to extend the `` element. Today, subsequent uses of the element after the initial one are ignored. Perhaps, named base URLs could be defined after the initial one and on anchor elements a `base` attribute could be used to indicate which base URL should be used. ```html Home Subsite Home ``` I’m not sure if a `base` attribute on `` elements would constitute as being backwards incompatible. I’m not married to the solution, it’s just what immediately comes to mind. ### Anything else? This is the discussion that prompted this request: https://fosstodon.org/@rauschma/112656258473960166
